orders.title: WO-036 — Walls and ways: the soldier scene gains walls and obstacles the operator draws on the field, a tile graph those block, A* and Dijkstra with the catalog's heuristics and cost functions as rail tools, path following with replanning when the field changes and a visible no-route state, obstacle and wall avoidance from the engine with a deterministic head-on policy, and geometry saved with the composition and replayed
orders.objective:
(the operator's session, WS-001 rule 24) the operator opens
the scene, chooses Draw wall and drags a wall across the field between the
units and the objective, then places two obstacles; they select a squad,
give it A* from the rail's new `ways` group and set the objective beyond the
wall; the units route around the wall's end, past the obstacles, and
arrive, the chosen unit's path drawn faintly ahead of it and the instruments
showing path length and replans; they turn on "show search" in the
inspector and see the cells the last search expanded; they drag another
wall across that path while the squad moves and watch the squad replan
around it; they close the gap entirely and read, in the inspector's notice
and in each unit's row of the text layer, that there is no route, the units
stopping where they are; they clear the walls and the squad moves again.
They give a second squad Obstacle and wall avoidance instead of a path and
watch it feel its way along the wall with its whiskers. They send two units
head on at each other and watch them part deterministically every time.
They save the composition, reload, open it, and the walls are there; they
run a trial with and without the wall from one seed and read the first
divergence. What the operator learns is how a route is found and followed
on a field with geometry, where it fails and what avoidance adds; what they
decide is whether a squad on this field is better served by a route or by
avoidance, and whether the cost functions need a cost layer to weigh.

orders.title: WO-024 — Concept studies V: levels, loops and teams, ten concepts from Gödel, Escher, Bach and ten from Team Topologies, each with a relations drawing, the two works whose vocabulary describes the platform itself
orders.objective:
(the operator's session, WS-001 rule 24) the operator opens
Tools, Catalog, chooses Gödel, Escher, Bach and sees ten studied concepts;
they open Levels of description and read its study: the idea in plain words
(the same system is truly described at several levels, each with its own
vocabulary, and no level is the real one) and a situation it serves (a
planning pass, an order, a gate row and a hook refusal are four descriptions
of one afternoon's work), a relations drawing they step through level by
level with the text equivalent naming each level and what it sees of the
next, the ordinary pseudocode of a chunking procedure, an illustrative RxJS
reading where a stream of low-level events becomes a stream of higher-level
ones, public treatments of the idea introduced on their own terms, the
references, the limits (a sealed-off level hides what leaks through) and the
nearby concepts as links (Chunking, Sealed-off levels, Strange loop). They
open Strange loop and step the drawing until it returns to where it began;
they open Isomorphism and Gödel numbering and see one idea become the other's
mechanism, with a small executable encoder they can read the spec of. They
choose Team Topologies, open Collaboration mode, X-as-a-Service mode and
Facilitating mode and read, in one drawing per mode, how two teams exchange
work and where each mode should end; they open Conway's law and read the
homomorphism the drawing shows between a team graph and a system graph, with
the Reverse Conway manoeuvre as its nearby inverse. What the operator learns
is the vocabulary for the levels the platform's mechanisms live on and the
modes its five roles work in; what they decide is which loop or mode to make
visible in the machinery view or a toy next.

## Goal-aligned decisions

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.



Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.

episode.statement: Independent plan refuter for one DotLn planning pass, using the Contra-Auguste mask and the architecture-and-semantics lens. I read the whole canonical refutation prompt that the parent supplied: identity, mask, lens, role, work order, output instructions, result schema and worker instructions. I also read its whole subject: the standard, whose theses, roles and capabilities are empty and which lists the vision, the roles document and the capability table as unavailable; the goal review, with its platform standard, goal-aligned-decisions standard, critical-path declaration and five cost-table trap observations; all eleven judged orders in full (title, objective, Cost line, non-goals and every criterion); the seventeen-order sequence; the empty deferrals; and the cost table (rows, traps and first verifications). The repository's operating contract and the host's session instructions were also in my context. I read no other repository file, no planner narrative, no earlier refutation receipt, no planning-pass document and nothing in the local control directory. I ran no test, gate or agent, and made no repository write or Git mutation. I wrote the result and this statement to the session scratch area, using a temporary schema-check script there that I then removed. Outcome: plan verdict aligned-with-findings, no holds, nine known issues. No vision passage was supplied and no observed trap shows worsening, so no order could be held. Model as the session context states it: claude-opus-5-5. Effort: not read back.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: It unblocks no foundation gate. The critical-path declaration lists WO-003 to WO-013 as closed and WO-008 as the only open foundation outcome, and says WO-008 does not gate the scene. WO-036 is a sandbox scene outcome. The sequence puts it first, following the 2026-10-24 placement of useful sandbox examples before authentication. Inside the horizon it is the prerequisite of WO-037 (bullets that walls and obstacles stop) and WO-045 (the grid family and A* study over the engine's own search), and its non-goals name both. NoOp cost in the records: the cost-table row for WO-036 has metrics null, so no record quantifies the NoOp, and the Cost line names only this pass's receipt as refutation paid. Doing nothing leaves the soldier scene without geometry and keeps twelve tools (the seven rows typed here and the five path.cost rows already typed) off the rail. It also leaves WO-037 and WO-045 unable to run as written.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: two of the order's own guards pull against each other. Criterion 3 requires engine changes so that two no-geometry crowd cases, which fail at the base, now pass. Criterion 2 requires the existing trial fixture's hashes unchanged 'so a run with no field step moves as it did' (known issue below). Elsewhere, the diff guard on the study directory and the background check on `aifg-a:247` protect WO-045's and the catalog's ground. Commons: it has the largest context estimate in the horizon: about 450 KB for the executor, about 50 files, 19 steps and 6 to 9 h plus design rounds. Five-size screenshots of a long walkthrough also cost verifier time. All of these are estimates, unknown until run. Drift: it raises the outcome bar, since rule 28 fails a sloppy or uncool scene and rule 29 fails a UI issue at the two large sizes. It does not normalize a worse baseline. Escalation: no tool script and no target command are added; one fixture joins an existing check. Success to the successful: Babylon.js (C2), navigation meshes and hierarchical search are excluded openly as candidates or non-goals, not silently. Burden: the design rounds need the operator's word to end or delay them (rule 25). Beyond that there is no recurring rescue. Rule beating: criterion 3 records both arms' exit codes at the base, and criterion 1 requires the verifier's own statement, so both resist passing without the behaviour. The 'so' clause of criterion 2 claims more than one fixture proves. Wrong goal: the session and its decision (route versus avoidance, and whether a cost layer is needed) are operator outcomes, not proxies. Observed rows over WO-033 to WO-039: machinery share fell from 0.66 to 0.23, operator directions were 0 for the last order, and no trap shows worsening or a reopen candidate. In the drift row, cold-start bytes grew for every role skill, with no ceiling set except the router's. That growth is on the kit side and no order here changes it. This order's own cost row is null, so its process cost is unknown, not failed. No vision passage was supplied, so no contradiction can be cited.
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost line says 'Removes nothing', against about 50 source files. These span the engine (four new modules and six extended), the schema enum, seven typed rows, the scene feature, fixtures, baselines and three documents, and the rail grows from sixteen tools to twenty-eight. For a product outcome in the target, the addition is the deliverable and no removal is owed. On the process side it adds one fixture to an existing check and no command, so nothing there needs offsetting. The Cost line does omit the crowd-settling and re-targeting change that criterion 3 requires of the engine (see the known issue).
orders.failureBehavior: Mostly it degrades to the old behaviour. When a field has no route, units stop, are marked `blocked` with a visible notice, and resume when the walls clear; nothing errors. A run with no field step is held to the base fixture's hashes. A trial saved before the new metrics existed restores with null series and is marked complete. The Collision avoidance study and the `avoid` function stay as they were. It still refuses a present series that is not numbers or null, which keeps the old guard. The exception is the one in the known issue: criterion 3 changes no-geometry crowd behaviour on purpose, so for those runs a failure of the new steering does not fall back to the old motion. Whether the base fixture covers such runs is unknown until activation.

findings.reason: Criterion 2 holds the hashes of `trial-known-outcome.json` equal to the base 'so a run with no field step moves as it did'. Criterion 3, however, requires two no-geometry engine cases that fail at the base to pass on the candidate: twelve units under priority steering with Arrive coming to rest, and a settled crowd, re-targeted, reaching its objective no later than plain Arrive. The objective's head-on policy also fires on a field with no walls. By construction, then, some runs with no field step move differently, and the 'so' clause is false in general. The two criteria can both pass only if the fixture's trial exercises neither change. The Cost line's steering entry names avoidance and the head-on policy but not the settling and re-targeting change.
findings.reopenWhen: At activation, the executor's run with the criterion-3 change alters any hash of `trial-known-outcome.json`, or the fixture's trial turns out to hold two or more units settling under priority steering with Arrive or meeting head on.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: It unblocks no foundation gate. It is the operator's study side work. The critical-path declaration says the concept-batch pass placed study batches at the front, and the sequence holds this order second. Inside the horizon it is the prerequisite of WO-032, which draws with the `relations` family this order lands. NoOp cost in the records: its cost-table row has metrics null. The Cost line records one earlier refutation paid (the 2026-10-30 second pass's receipt, on the text before amendment) plus this pass's. Doing nothing leaves Gödel, Escher, Bach and Team Topologies unstudied and the `relations` family unbuilt, and it leaves WO-032 blocked.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: none observed in the text. The ban on per-study presentation modules (the grep must print 0) and the shared builder keep the family from forking per study. Commons: about 80 source files plus twenty records, about 250 KB for the executor, and a parallel author fan-out whose worker and session totals are recorded outside acceptance. All unknown until run. Drift: rule 27's random sample of five records, judged for quality, and rule 29's two large sizes raise the bar rather than lower it. Escalation: no new command. The coverage rows and the `relations` rule are target documents, not new gates. Success to the successful: the family follows the three existing builders, which is reuse, not exclusion, and the design pair sets a ring against a stack. Burden: the design rounds need the operator's word (rule 25); no other recurring rescue. Rule beating: criterion 7's grep proves only that the token `relationsModel` appears in the rules file. The behaviour is carried by criterion 3's specs and criterion 1's own-words statement, so the grep is not the evidence of record. Wrong goal: the objective names what the operator learns (the vocabulary of levels and modes in which the platform's roles work) and what they decide (which loop or mode to show next). Observed traps over WO-033 to WO-039 show no worsening and no reopen candidate. This order's process cost is unknown, not failed. No vision passage was supplied, so no contradiction can be cited.
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost line says 'Removes nothing', against a new family (builder, model type, view, mapper branch and composite) and twenty records with their message catalogs and chunks. For product content in the target, no removal is owed, and the process side adds no command.
orders.failureBehavior: It degrades. The records and the family load in lazy chunks, so existing works and their studies are untouched. A study without a drawing or mechanism carries `visual: null` or `executable: null` with its reason and renders without it; the page does not fail. The study check refuses an incomplete record at the gate. That is a check refusing a candidate, not the running app refusing the operator.
